newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi says would prefer communists in govt.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says would prefer communists in govt.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday he would prefer his parliamentary ally the hard-left Communist Refoundation party to be part of his centre-left government because it would show common commitment.
"I'd prefer (Refoundation leader Fausto) Bertinotti inside the government because that would mean sharing the collective responsibility," Prodi told a talk show on state television RAI.
"But we would need clear, precise, long-term agreements, because governing is no joke."

Bertinotti said earlier in Milan that, even though France's Socialists had asked communists to join their new left government after their stunning election victory, he did not foresee his party joining Prodi's Olive Tree alliance.
"Our programmes are too far apart," Bertinotti told reporters who asked whether Refoundation was closer to taking a place in government after the French experience.
Prodi relies upon Refoundation for a parliamentary majority and the two sides have had a strained relationship since Prodi took office in May 1996.

Bertinotti's refusal to back the deployment of an Italian-led security force for Albania almost caused Prodi's government to fall in April and Refoundation has already signalled tough opposition to any cuts in social spending.
Prodi is due to begin talks on reform of the welfare state later this month.
